title: Dual Disruption in Mesh Topology: Coordination & Connectivity Stress Test
description: This scenario explores dual disruption dynamics within a mesh communication topology. The disturbance creates coordination challenges that test the agents' ability to adapt, communicate effectively via multi-hop relay, and maintain freight flow under adverse conditions where both logical (agent connectivity) and physical (infrastructure) constraints occur simultaneously.

disruption_1.description: Agent 'a' loses ability to broadcast/relay messages, becoming an isolated node or a silent participant in the mesh.

disruption_2.description: Physical link between east and south is severed, forcing rerouting through north or west.

edge_cases_to_watch: Communication loss coincides with physical route closure
Agents cannot coordinate about the bridge closure
Recovery requires handling both disruptions simultaneously
Network Partitioning: If agent 'a' was a critical relay between 'b' and 'c', the mesh splits into two sub-graphs
Information Asymmetry: Agent 'a' knows about the bridge closure but cannot communicate it to the rest of the mesh
Congestion Cascades: Rerouting 'east-south' traffic through 'north' exceeds capacity of 'east-north' route
coordination_challenges: Dynamic Topology Awareness: Maintaining a consistent belief state of the network when agents cannot talk to each other
Multi-hop Routing Reliability: Determining if a message can actually reach a destination through remaining agents
Conflict Resolution: Handling two agents attempting to use the single-capacity 'east-north' route during a crisis
Delayed Consensus: Achieving agreement on new freight routes when the communication latency or packet loss increases due to relay-loss
suggested_agent_strategies: Gossip-based Information Dissemination: Using epidemic protocols to spread news of bridge closures via any available neighbor
Predictive Rerouting: Agents should simulate potential route failures and preemptively move to buffer depots
Redundant Messaging: Sending critical job updates through multiple paths in the mesh to mitigate the impact of agent 'a' failure
Role Assumption: If a primary relay agent fails, other agents must elect a new coordination leader to manage the high-priority 'j-004' and 'j-001' jobs

success_criteria: Agents adapt communication to topology constraints
Recovery from disruption within expected turns
Minimal capacity violations on single-capacity routes
